newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar tells private firms to hire more nationals.
newsitem.headline: Qatar tells private firms to hire more nationals.

text.p: Qatar has told private companies and banks in the Gulf Arab state to make sure that at least 20 percent of their staff are Qatari nationals, newspapers said on Tuesday.
Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani issued the directive as part of Qatar's efforts to curb the high number of expatriates in its workforce.

Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain -- have launched a drive to find more jobs for their citizens in an attempt to reduce dependence on millions of expatriates who help them run their economies.
The directive, published in newspapers, is also applicable to semi-government-owned firms and banks operating in Qatar.
Qatar has a native population of around 160,000 and a total population of 650,000, including expatriate workers who make up about 90 percent of the workforce.
The private sector employs 80 percent of Qatar's workforce of about 200,000.
